finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll(). rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sending a request to the purge endpoint
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the requesting user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, so there is no early return or 403

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm has no side effects and does not write a response (handlers.go:12-14). No middleware or other file exists in the repo to enforce authorization. The only other check in the repo is mustPerm in rotateKeys (handlers.go:33), which is correct. Not applied to purge.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware or other files exist in the repo)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u,"admin") as a bare statement and discards the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys, which returns on a failed mustPerm at handlers.go:33-35.
